details.label: Summary
details.text: Wind-damage potential will spread east-southeastward with an ongoing storm cluster, though longevity of the threat is uncertain

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A small southeastward-moving storm cluster has evolved across west-central IN, with another isolated strong to potentially severe storm ongoing north of Indianapolis. This somewhat elevated convection has developed north of an outflow-reinforced front, within a low-level warm-advection regime that will continue for much of the overnight. MUCAPE of 1000-2000 J/kg and 30-40 kt of effective shear will continue to support organized storms. The modest upscale growth noted across west-central IN could lead to an increase in wind-damage potential over the next 1-2 hours. However, the magnitude of the threat is uncertain due to lingering near-surface stability, and recent objective mesoanalyses depict decreasing MUCAPE and increasing MUCINH with southeastward extent. If a robust cold pool can become established, then a more organized wind-damage threat could evolve across a larger portion of central IN with time. Otherwise, localized strong/damaging gusts will continue to be possible, and some potential for isolated hail may persist with the remaining semi-discrete cells
